title: Grant, expire or revoke a permission set
lede: {{castAName}} is granted {{castPermSet}} for a window and loses it again: by deleting the policy (observed) or, in this lab, when the window closes (lab-invented). Steps marked lab-invented are not from the guide. Simulated; hosts are examples.

steps.title: Grant for a window
steps.what: The admin grants {{castPermSet}} to {{castAName}} through a policy with a duration. The default Privilege offered was about a year, so pick the shortest to show expiry. Some sets are refused: one that needs a permission set license, one under another user licence, one the user already holds.

steps.title: The assignment is made in Salesforce
steps.what: Privilege signs in and assigns the permission set to the user. In Salesforce the user's Permission Set Assignments lists it.

steps.title: A receipt says Granted
steps.what: Access Receipts shows user, set, end date and status Granted, and the reconciliation line reads 1 confirmed.

steps.title: The reaper removes access when the window closes
steps.what: LAB-INVENTED: when the window on the lab clock closes, the lab removes the assignment by itself. The guide observed removal only by deleting the policy.

steps.title: Delete the policy: Revoke pending
steps.what: There is no Revoke button: the admin deletes the policy. The receipt reads Revoke pending, access still live, and the assignment is still in Salesforce.

steps.title: The next reconcile or Sync removes the assignment
steps.what: The assignment is removed in Salesforce and the policy count drops to 0, Expired / Revoked shows 1. LAB-INVENTED: that the next reconcile or Sync is what clears it; the guide observed it clearing after a wait.

steps.title: The receipt moves to Expired / Revoked
steps.what: Access Receipts shows the policy under Expired / Revoked: the policy count drops to 0 and Expired / Revoked shows 1.

steps.title: Reconcile finds access assigned by hand
steps.what: LAB-INVENTED: access an admin assigns by hand in Salesforce is found by a reconcile; the lab calls it discovered, or orphaned if Privilege once granted it, and lets you revoke it. The product's own wording and handling were not observed.
